_comment: EXAMPLE MISSION -- edit this file to define YOUR route order.
This encodes the sequence you described: mud course -> turn -> slopes
-> avoid compost pit -> gravel -> cement -> choose court or pathway.
Each stage = behaviour + exit test + guards. Behaviours:
follow      : camera-guided open-surface following (the normal mode)
pivot_left  : turn in place left  (open-loop, timed)
pivot_right : turn in place right (open-loop, timed)
creep       : follow, but slowly (for steps, ramps, gravel)
straight    : ignore steering, drive straight (short bursts only)
Exit tests (first one that fires wins; timeout_s is the safety net):
surface: mud|gravel|cement|grass   + hold_s   (must persist)
marker : name from vision/landmarks.MARKER_COLOURS. NOTHING IS PLACED
ON THE COURSE -- these are colour cues from objects already
there (the green compost sacks, the blue toilets), so treat
them as a bonus and always leave a timeout_s behind them.
landmark: name registered in the LandmarkBook
obstacle_within_m: ultrasonic distance
timeout_s: seconds
keepout_bias: constant steer offset (+right/-left). Use when a hazard is
always on one known side, e.g. grass embankment always on the right.
_zones_note: MEASURED from the site photos, not guessed. rough_n is the texture axis
(0=glass-smooth, 1=very rough): it is what separates the smooth cement
slab from grey gravel chippings, which colour alone cannot do.
Re-measure for your own conditions with:

stages.name: mud_course
stages.notes: Drive the length of the mud court. Grass embankment is on the RIGHT (see Photos/IMG20260728121844.jpg) so bias gently LEFT. The court itself has ~30% grass tufts - that is drivable, not a keep-out.

stages.name: turn_to_slopes
stages.notes: A SIMPLE ~90 deg turn, not a U-turn. Open-loop timed pivot: error scales with the angle, so a quarter turn drifts about a quarter as much as a half turn did, and the next stage steers on the camera anyway - no IMU needed. CALIBRATE THE TIME ON THE DAY'S SURFACE: pivot for 5 s at speed 0.55, count the turns, divide. 1.3 s assumes ~70 deg/s, which is what the old 2.6 s half-turn implied. Grip and battery charge both change it, so re-time it on site.

stages.name: slopes
stages.notes: Sloped/embankment section. Higher speed = more torque for the climb; creep behaviour keeps steering gentle so the car does not slew sideways across the slope.

stages.name: avoid_compost_pit
stages.notes: The compost pit is an EXCAVATED HOLE (Photos/IMG20260728133107.jpg) - a negative obstacle the FORWARD ultrasonic cannot see and the camera cannot see either. Defence in depth: bias right for the whole stage, exit on the bright-green sacks that flank the pit (they are already on site - nothing is placed), and fall back to the timeout. THE SPEED IS DELIBERATELY LOW: with the downward sensor fitted, this is the stage where its ~0.5 s of warning has to be enough, and speed 0.50 keeps the car inside it. Without that sensor nothing detects the pit at all and the bias plus a wide berth are all you have.

stages.name: gravel_crossing
stages.notes: Loose gravel - low traction, wheels sink. Slow + high torque. Surface reads ~0.87 hard / low saturation.

stages.name: cross_onto_cement
stages.notes: The dirt-to-cement edge. It is a sharp 6-10cm lip in places (Photos/IMG20260729132039.jpg) and nearly flush in others (Photos/IMG20260729132145.jpg) - the SAME edge. The car squares up first, then bursts across with momentum. With the downward sensor fitted the burst waits until the ground actually reads short, i.e. until the lip is really there; without it the car bursts as soon as it is squared up, because no camera can see a 6cm step. Keep this stage SHORT; if it times out the car simply carries on.

stages.name: cement_run
stages.notes: On the cement apron/pathway. Final stage - choose the pathway rather than the court by biasing away from the court edge (keepout_bias), since with nothing placed on the course there is no marker to pick the branch with. If the two branches differ underfoot, a surface exit can split them; otherwise this is an open-loop choice and the bias is what makes it.
